request.prompt:
Job X1: usp_broker_production (tsql), file estate/holdout/X1_usp_broker_production.sql.
Broker and line-of-business production as at the as-of date (policies in force, EUR written premium, claims notified and paid in the year, paid-to-written review flag)

Code:
  1 | /*==============================================================================
  2 |   Job      : rpt.usp_broker_production
  3 |   Purpose  : Broker production report for distribution MI. One row per broker
  4 |              and line of business as at @AsOfDate: policies in force, gross
  5 |              written premium in EUR booked in the calendar year, claims notified
  6 |              and claims paid in the year, and a review flag for brokers whose
  7 |              paid-to-written ratio for the year is above 0.75.
  8 |   Author   : PdeB
  9 |   Change log
 10 |     2014-02-10  PdeB  Initial version (CR-0412)
 11 |     2015-09-03  PdeB  GBP/USD premium converted to EUR at the ECB rate (CR-0688)
 12 |     2017-11-20  SOK   Direct business reported under broker code DIRECT (CR-1047)
 13 |     2019-05-14  AMcG  Inactive brokers kept when they still have business (INC-2231)
 14 |     2021-03-08  SOK   Paid-to-written review flag for distribution (CR-1590)
 15 |     2022-06-27  AMcG  Broker codes trimmed and upper-cased (INC-3118)
 16 | ==============================================================================*/
 17 | SET NOCOUNT ON;
 18 | GO
 19 | IF OBJECT_ID(N'rpt.broker_production', N'U') IS NULL
 20 | CREATE TABLE rpt.broker_production (
 21 |     as_of_date         DATE           NOT NULL,
 22 |     broker_code        VARCHAR(10)    NOT NULL,
 23 |     broker_name        NVARCHAR(80)   NULL,
 24 |     broker_status      VARCHAR(10)    NULL,
 25 |     lob_code           VARCHAR(5)     NOT NULL,
 26 |     policies_in_force  INT            NOT NULL,
 27 |     gwp_eur            DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 28 |     claims_notified    INT            NOT NULL,
 29 |     claims_paid_eur    DECIMAL(14,2)  NOT NULL,
 30 |     paid_to_written    DECIMAL(12,4)  NULL,
 31 |     review_flag        CHAR(1)        NOT NULL
 32 | );
 33 | GO
 34 | CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE rpt.usp_broker_production
 35 |     @AsOfDate DATE
 36 | AS
 37 | BEGIN
 38 |     SET NOCOUNT ON;
 39 | 
 40 |     DECLARE @job       VARCHAR(128) = 'rpt.usp_broker_production';
 41 |     DECLARE @YearStart DATE         = DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(@AsOfDate), 1, 1);
 42 |     DECLARE @rows      INT;
 43 | 
 44 |     BEGIN TRY
 45 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'start', @status = 'STARTED';
 46 | 
 47 |         -- policy attributes from the latest snapshot on or before the as-of date
 48 |         SELECT x.policy_id, x.broker_code, x.lob_code, x.inception_date, x.expiry_date, x.cancellation_date
 49 |         INTO #pol
 50 |         FROM (
 51 |             SELECT s.policy_id,
 52 |                    ISNULL(UPPER(LTRIM(RTRIM(s.broker_code))), 'DIRECT') AS broker_code,
 53 |                    UPPER(RTRIM(p.lob_code)) AS lob_code,
 54 |                    s.inception_date, s.expiry_date, s.cancellation_date,
 55 |                    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.policy_id
 56 |                                       ORDER BY s.snapshot_date DESC, s._row_seq DESC) AS rn
 57 |             FROM stg.policy_snapshots s WITH (NOLOCK)
 58 |             INNER JOIN stg.products p WITH (NOLOCK) ON p.product_code = s.product_code
 59 |             WHERE s.snapshot_date <= @AsOfDate
 60 |         ) x
 61 |         WHERE x.rn = 1;
 62 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 63 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'policies', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 64 | 
 65 |         -- policies in force on the as-of date
 66 |         SELECT p.broker_code, p.lob_code, COUNT(*) AS policies_in_force
 67 |         INTO #inforce
 68 |         FROM #pol p
 69 |         WHERE p.inception_date <= @AsOfDate
 70 |           AND p.expiry_date >= @AsOfDate
 71 |           AND (p.cancellation_date IS NULL OR p.cancellation_date > @AsOfDate)
 72 |         GROUP BY p.broker_code, p.lob_code;
 73 | 
 74 |         -- premium booked in the year, at the latest rate published on or before the booking date
 75 |         SELECT p.broker_code, p.lob_code,
 76 |                SUM(t.amount * CASE WHEN t.currency = 'EUR' THEN 1 ELSE fx.rate_to_eur END) AS gwp_eur
 77 |         INTO #gwp
 78 |         FROM stg.premium_transactions t WITH (NOLOCK)
 79 |         INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = t.policy_id
 80 |         OUTER APPLY (
 81 |             SELECT TOP 1 f.rate_to_eur
 82 |             FROM stg.fx_rates f WITH (NOLOCK)
 83 |             WHERE f.currency = t.currency
 84 |               AND f.rate_date <= t.txn_date
 85 |             ORDER BY f.rate_date DESC, f._row_seq DESC
 86 |         ) fx
 87 |         WHERE t.txn_date >= @YearStart
 88 |           AND t.txn_date <= @AsOfDate
 89 |         GROUP BY p.broker_code, p.lob_code;
 90 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
 91 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'premium', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
 92 | 
 93 |         -- claims notified in the year
 94 |         SELECT c.claim_id, p.broker_code, p.lob_code
 95 |         INTO #clm
 96 |         FROM stg.claims c WITH (NOLOCK)
 97 |         INNER JOIN #pol p ON p.policy_id = c.policy_id
 98 |         WHERE c.reported_date >= @YearStart
 99 |           AND c.reported_date <= @AsOfDate;
100 | 
101 |         SELECT c.broker_code, c.lob_code, COUNT(*) AS claims_notified
102 |         INTO #notified
103 |         FROM #clm c
104 |         GROUP BY c.broker_code, c.lob_code;
105 | 
106 |         -- claims paid in the year, recoveries netted off, unkeyed amounts ignored
107 |         SELECT c.broker_code, c.lob_code, SUM(ISNULL(cp.amount, 0)) AS claims_paid_eur
108 |         INTO #paid
109 |         FROM stg.claim_payments cp WITH (NOLOCK)
110 |         INNER JOIN #clm c ON c.claim_id = cp.claim_id
111 |         WHERE cp.payment_date >= @YearStart
112 |           AND cp.payment_date <= @AsOfDate
113 |         GROUP BY c.broker_code, c.lob_code;
114 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
115 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'claims', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
116 | 
117 |         SELECT broker_code, lob_code INTO #keys FROM #inforce
118 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #gwp
119 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #notified
120 |         UNION SELECT broker_code, lob_code FROM #paid;
121 | 
122 |         -- paid-to-written ratio over all lines of the broker
123 |         SELECT k.broker_code,
124 |                CAST(SUM(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0)) / NULLIF(SUM(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0)), 0) AS DECIMAL(12,4)) AS paid_to_written
125 |         INTO #ratio
126 |         FROM #keys k
127 |         LEFT JOIN #gwp g   ON g.broker_code = k.broker_code AND g.lob_code = k.lob_code
128 |         LEFT JOIN #paid pd ON pd.broker_code = k.broker_code AND pd.lob_code = k.lob_code
129 |         GROUP BY k.broker_code;
130 | 
131 |         TRUNCATE TABLE rpt.broker_production;
132 | 
133 |         INSERT INTO rpt.broker_production
134 |             (as_of_date, broker_code, broker_name, broker_status, lob_code, policies_in_force,
135 |              gwp_eur, claims_notified, claims_paid_eur, paid_to_written, review_flag)
136 |         SELECT @AsOfDate,
137 |                k.broker_code,
138 |                b.broker_name,
139 |                UPPER(RTRIM(b.status)),
140 |                k.lob_code,
141 |                ISNULL(i.policies_in_force, 0),
142 |                CAST(ISNULL(g.gwp_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),
143 |                ISNULL(n.claims_notified, 0),
144 |                CAST(ISNULL(pd.claims_paid_eur, 0) AS DECIMAL(14,2)),
145 |                r.paid_to_written,
146 |                CASE WHEN r.paid_to_written > 0.75 THEN 'Y' ELSE 'N' END
147 |         FROM #keys k
148 |         LEFT JOIN stg.brokers b WITH (NOLOCK) ON b.broker_code = k.broker_code
149 |         LEFT JOIN #inforce i  ON i.broker_code = k.broker_code AND i.lob_code = k.lob_code
150 |         LEFT JOIN #gwp g      ON g.broker_code = k.broker_code AND g.lob_code = k.lob_code
151 |         LEFT JOIN #notified n ON n.broker_code = k.broker_code AND n.lob_code = k.lob_code
152 |         LEFT JOIN #paid pd    ON pd.broker_code = k.broker_code AND pd.lob_code = k.lob_code
153 |         LEFT JOIN #ratio r    ON r.broker_code = k.broker_code;
154 |         SET @rows = @@ROWCOUNT;
155 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'load rpt.broker_production', @status = 'INFO', @rows_affected = @rows;
156 | 
157 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'SUCCESS';
158 |     END TRY
159 |     BEGIN CATCH
160 |         DECLARE @msg NVARCHAR(4000) = ERROR_MESSAGE(), @err INT = ERROR_NUMBER();
161 |         EXEC etl.usp_log_step @job_name = @job, @step_name = 'end', @status = 'FAILED',
162 |              @message = @msg, @error_number = @err;
163 |         THROW;
164 |     END CATCH
165 | END;
166 | GO

Trap cards:
- TSQL-01 (semantic) Case-insensitive collation in =, IN, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and joins. Legacy: Under a case-insensitive collation such as SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text compares equal regardless of letter case (and of trailing spaces, see TSQL-02): state = 'ACTIVE' also matches 'Active' and 'active'; GROUP BY, DISTINCT, PARTITION BY and join keys put case variants together. The stored value is returned unchanged. Spark: Spark compares strings in binary order: 'Active' <> 'ACTIVE', so a filter drops case variants, a GROUP BY splits them into separate groups and a join misses them.
- TSQL-02 (semantic) Comparisons ignore trailing spaces; CHAR(n) pads with spaces. Legacy: SQL Server pads the shorter string with spaces before comparing, so 'WEST ' = 'WEST' (also in IN, GROUP BY and joins). CHAR(n) and NCHAR(n) values are stored and returned padded to n characters: 'AB' in a CHAR(4) column is 'AB '. LEN() ignores trailing spaces (TSQL-15). Leading spaces always count. Spark: Spark compares strings exactly, so 'WEST ' <> 'WEST', and its string type never pads. A value read from a CHAR source column keeps whatever spaces it was stored with.
- TSQL-03 (semantic) Integer division truncates. Legacy: INT / INT is integer division in T-SQL, truncating toward zero: 7 / 2 = 3, -7 / 2 = -3. The result type follows the operands, so the fraction is lost before any later cast, e.g. CAST(qty / pack_size AS DECIMAL(9,2)) or 100 * a / b. Spark: Spark's / always returns a double (7 / 2 = 3.5); DIV is integer division.
- TSQL-04 (semantic) DATEDIFF counts boundaries crossed, not elapsed periods. Legacy: DATEDIFF(datepart, a, b) counts the datepart boundaries crossed between a and b: DATEDIFF(year, '2025-12-31', '2026-01-01') = 1 and DATEDIFF(month, '2025-01-31', '2025-02-01') = 1. DATEDIFF(week, ...) counts Sundays crossed, whatever SET DATEFIRST says. DATEDIFF(day, ...) on DATE values equals the day difference. Spark: datediff(end, start) counts days (arguments reversed); months_between returns a fraction with its own month-end rule; floor(months/12) counts elapsed years, not boundaries.
- TSQL-05 (semantic) + concatenation with NULL yields NULL. Legacy: With CONCAT_NULL_YIELDS_NULL ON (the default), 'A' + NULL is NULL, so a whole concatenation is NULL when any part is. CONCAT() and CONCAT_WS() treat NULL as empty. Spark: Spark's + is arithmetic only; concat() returns NULL when any argument is NULL, while concat_ws() skips NULLs and format_string writes 'null'.
- TSQL-06 (semantic) ISNULL takes the type of its first argument; NULL treated as equal in change checks. Legacy: ISNULL(a, b) returns a's data type, so the replacement b is converted to it: a VARCHAR(5) column with ISNULL(col, 'UNKNOWN') returns 'UNKNO' (truncated), and ISNULL(int_col, 0.5) returns 0. COALESCE uses the highest-precedence type instead. Change detection written as ISNULL(src, '') <> ISNULL(tgt, '') treats NULL and '' as the same value. Spark: coalesce() keeps the replacement as written ('UNKNOWN') and widens types; it never truncates.
- TSQL-07 (semantic) DECIMAL precision and scale, and ROUND on computed values. Legacy: DECIMAL arithmetic follows fixed precision and scale rules (e.g. division keeps at least 6 decimal places, results are capped at 38 digits and the scale shrinks to fit); intermediate results are rounded at each step to their result type. ROUND(x, n) rounds half away from zero; ROUND(x, n, 1) truncates. Assigning to a DECIMAL(p,s) column rounds. Spark: Spark's decimal rules are similar but not identical (scale reduction, and doubles if an operand is a double literal); F.round on a double rounds the binary value, so a computed 2.675 (really 2.67499...) rounds to 2.67; bround is half-even.
- TSQL-08 (semantic) TOP and TOP WITH TIES. Legacy: TOP n returns n rows in ORDER BY order (arbitrary among ties unless the ORDER BY is unique); TOP n WITH TIES also returns every row tied with the last one. Spark: limit(n) after orderBy returns exactly n rows; ties need a rank window.
- TSQL-09 (construct) CROSS APPLY / OUTER APPLY with TOP 1. Legacy: CROSS APPLY (SELECT TOP 1 ... WHERE inner.k = outer.k ORDER BY ...) picks one inner row per outer row and drops outer rows with no match; OUTER APPLY keeps them with NULLs. Spark: Spark has no APPLY; a lateral subquery or a window replaces it.
- TSQL-10 (construct) UPDATE ... FROM. Legacy: UPDATE t SET ... FROM t JOIN s ON ... updates each target row from one matching source row; with several matches, which one wins is undefined. Spark: DataFrames are immutable; an update becomes a join plus a select.
- TSQL-11 (construct) MERGE and type-2 history. Legacy: MERGE matches target and source rows and updates, inserts or deletes in one statement. Type-2 history closes the current version (valid_to, is_current) of changed rows and inserts a new current version; IDENTITY keys are assigned in the INSERT's ORDER BY order, continuing from the table's highest value. Spark: Spark has no MERGE on DataFrames (Delta MERGE exists for tables); the job must compute the new state as a whole table from the previous state and the batch.
- TSQL-12 (construct) Cursors and WHILE loops. Legacy: A cursor processes rows one at a time in its ORDER BY order; variables carry state between rows (running totals, last values). NULL arithmetic inside the loop propagates: SET @total = @total + NULL makes @total NULL for the rest of the loop. Spark: Spark is set-based; loops become aggregations or ordered windows.
- TSQL-13 (construct) Temp tables. Legacy: #temp tables hold intermediate results for the session. Spark: Intermediate results are DataFrames or temporary views.
- TSQL-14 (semantic) LIKE character classes. Legacy: T-SQL LIKE supports character classes: '[0-9]' matches one digit, '[A-Z]' one letter (case-insensitively under a CI collation), '[^0-9]' a non-digit; % and _ as usual. Spark: Spark's LIKE has only % and _; '[0-9]' matches the literal text '[0-9]'.
- TSQL-15 (semantic) LEN ignores trailing spaces; SUBSTRING from 0; LEFT and RIGHT. Legacy: LEN(x) does not count trailing spaces (DATALENGTH does). SUBSTRING(x, 0, n) returns n-1 characters, because position 0 is before the string. LEFT/RIGHT count characters. Spark: length() counts trailing spaces; substring(x, 0, n) is treated like position 1 and returns n characters.
- TSQL-16 (semantic) CONVERT style codes. Legacy: CONVERT(type, date, style) formats dates by style: 101 mm/dd/yyyy, 103 dd/mm/yyyy, 104 dd.mm.yyyy, 105 dd-mm-yyyy, 106 dd mon yyyy, 111 yyyy/mm/dd, 112 yyyymmdd, 120 yyyy-mm-dd hh:mi:ss, 121 with milliseconds, 23 yyyy-mm-dd. Converting into a shorter CHAR(n)/VARCHAR(n) silently keeps the first n characters: CONVERT(CHAR(6), d, 112) is yyyymm. Spark: A cast to string gives yyyy-MM-dd; date_format needs a Java pattern; nothing truncates.
- TSQL-17 (construct) PIVOT. Legacy: PIVOT (aggregate(value) FOR col IN ([a], [b])) groups by every other column of the source and turns listed values into columns; values not listed are dropped; missing combinations give NULL. Spark: groupBy(...).pivot(col, values).agg(...) does the same when the values are listed; the grouping columns must be stated explicitly.
- TSQL-18 (semantic) EOMONTH and DATEADD at month-end. Legacy: DATEADD(month, n, d) clamps to the last day of the target month: DATEADD(month, 1, '2024-01-31') = '2024-02-29'; adding months to an earlier date never moves to a month-end. EOMONTH(d, n) returns the last day of the month n months away. Spark: add_months clamps the same way but also moves a last-day-of-month input to the target month's last day (add_months('2024-02-29', 1) = '2024-03-31'); last_day(d) is EOMONTH.
- TSQL-19 (semantic) Text ordering under collations (accents, case) in ORDER BY, MIN, MAX and rankings. Legacy: Under SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS, text sorts case-insensitively with accent rules (Á sorts with A); MIN/MAX on text and ORDER BY text in a ranking follow that order. Spark: Spark sorts strings by code point: 'Zoe' < 'aoife' and 'Á' sorts after 'Z'.

findings.note: The products join compares the raw VARCHAR product_code values without any normalisation. Under the CI collation, case variants match; in Spark they would not, so policies would drop out of the inner join.
The product_code join ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark needs an rtrim on both sides or padded codes miss the inner join.
t.currency is CHAR(3) text, so currency = 'EUR' also matches 'eur'/'Eur' under the CI collation. A binary comparison in Spark would route those rows to the fx rate instead.
currency is CHAR(3) and the comparison ignores trailing spaces (e.g. 'EUR ' or a padded short code). Spark compares exactly.
The fx lookup matches f.currency = t.currency, two text columns from different sources, case-insensitively. In Spark, case variants would find no rate and the premium would come out NULL.
The CHAR(3) currency match ignores trailing spaces in SQL Server. Spark matches exactly unless both sides are trimmed.
OUTER APPLY TOP 1 picks the latest fx rate on or before txn_date and keeps transactions that have no rate. In Spark this must become a left join plus a row_number window.
TOP 1 ordered by rate_date DESC, _row_seq DESC. The order is deterministic as long as _row_seq is unique per date, and the Spark window must use the same tie-break.

DECIMAL(38,2)/DECIMAL(38,2) division is cut down to scale 6 in SQL Server and then rounded to DECIMAL(12,4), so the value is rounded twice. Spark's decimal division and cast must give the same ratio, which feeds the 0.75 flag.
amount DECIMAL(12,2) * rate DECIMAL(18,8), summed. The result's precision and scale must match legacy before the final rounding to 2dp.
The high-scale gwp sum is cast to DECIMAL(14,2), rounding half away from zero. Spark must cast the decimal and must not round a double.
Claims paid is cast to DECIMAL(14,2). Spark must keep decimal types (not double) so the result matches.
stg.brokers.broker_code is not normalised, but k.broker_code is upper-cased. The CI join still matches lower- or mixed-case broker codes; a binary Spark join would lose broker_name and status.

stg.brokers.broker_code is CHAR(6), so it is padded with spaces and may also carry stored trailing spaces. SQL Server's join ignores them, while Spark needs rtrim on b.broker_code to match the trimmed key.
